graphEvents.label: The Flow handoff is one-way and terminal
Artifact export and board read-back are incompatible completions
Story Mode forbids images and invented links

label: Routing is correctly two-stage: the hub selects one of four modes, ROUTER.md maps intent to packet-qualified leaves, and the packet Section 2 routes inside the packet.
Flow is a sibling route with its own leaf set of flow-mode and flow-templates, after which the FigJam packet adds the chosen type reference and template.
The handoff is prose, not a resolvable resource: the Product Owner map keeps a FLOW lane that a guard drops, and Section 2 hands the route to the other packet.
The two halves have incompatible completion protocols: artifacts save to export before replying, while Flow is the sole exemption and answers with a board URL, read-back, Left out and self-scan.
The Flow reply is terminal and carries the board, its proof and the self-scan and nothing else, so a produced board URL has no route back into the request that motivated it.
An artifact word beats FigJam framing: FigJam beside another artifact is that artifact subject, so a runbook with a FigJam process never loads Flow Mode and the diagram is never produced.
Doc Mode preserves supplied diagrams as text but has no instruction to commission a board or insert a board link, which is the doc-first pattern the corpus already documents.
Story Mode never invents a Figma destination and forbids images or image paths in a Story or Epic, so a board URL returned later in the session cannot legally be carried.
The registry records no handoff shape for the FigJam mode: it declares backend, tools, packet and aliases, with no input, artifact served or write-back field.
Stage one refuses ordered bundles by design, so a Story plus its flow costs a disambiguation question even when the order is obvious.
A Flow request naming an artifact crosses the hub skill, the packet router and the Flow packet before any type guidance loads, and no artifact context is carried across.
ClickUp is a separate vendored transport and templates defer images to ClickUp embedding, so a generated board can only travel as a link in the artifact References groups, never an attachment.
